sections.content: How many people are "natural and social science professionals (other)"?

19,480 people

were counted on the census as "natural and social science professionals (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.
People who do this type of work perform a variety of scientific research and related activities not elsewhere classified.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "natural and social science professionals (other)", 18.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "natural and social science professionals (other)" was 16 to 19 years.

  • physiotherapists
  • arts officers, producers and directors
  • speech and language therapists

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "natural and social science professionals (other)" there were more men than women (58.2% compared with 41.8%).

This means "natural and social science professionals (other)" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, research, engineering and technology professionals".

Men made up 58.2% and women made up 41.8% of "natural and social science professionals (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "natural and social science professionals (other)" included:

  • arts officers, producers and directors
  • stock control clerks and assistants
  • specialist medical practitioners

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "natural and social science professionals (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "natural and social science professionals (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "natural and social science professionals (other)", 7.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (90% compared with 10%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.9%) than self-employed (4.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cambridge, this is in the region of the East of England.
